newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Irish presidency sets out farm programme.
newsitem.headline: EU Irish presidency sets out farm programme.

text.p: Irish farm minister Ivan Yates on Tuesday set out the priorities for his country's programme as European Union president in an address to Euro-MPs, pledging to tackle the beef sector and to make progress in reform of several sectors of the Common Agricultrual Policy.

In a speech to the European Parliament's agriculture committee he said Ireland would be seeking agreement on a number of veterinary measures mainly focused on food safety and animal health and welfare, including trading rules.
Detailing the sectoral reforms he aims for, Yates said they included wine, bananas, olive oil and tobacco, for which formal proposals were expected.
He said he wants to see a common organisation in the market for potatoes on which he will be opening new discussions following earlier failure to reach agreement.
He said that Ireland was committeed to animal health and welfare and wanted to see finalisation of the proposal to update the EU drective on internal trade in cattle and pigs adopted 30 years ago.

Stressing his country's commitment to EU enlargement he said that the presidency would be opening a "structured dialogue" with the applicant countries and would set up a high level group to prepare further contacts at ministerial level.
"Our approach to the question of future accession of the applicant countries is probably the most important matter that will have to be dealt with over the months and years ahead," he said.
